{{short description|German herpetologist (born 1955)}}
[[File:Monitor Lizard, Sungei Buloh Wetlands Reserve, Singapore (1669835154).jpg|thumb|Asian water monitor ([[Asian water monitor|''Varanus salvator'']])]]
'''Maren Birgit Gaulke''' (born 4 April 1955) is a German [[herpetologist]] whose research focus has been the biology of monitor lizards, snakes, and turtles. She is a consultant with national and international institutions and contributes to status classifications of endangered species and the establishment of protected areas.

==Biography==
A student of earth and life sciences, Gaulke received her doctorate from the [[Kiel University|University of Kiel]] in 1988. In the mid-1980s she began her field work in [[Southeast Asia]] and the [[Philippines]], where her biological studies collected new insights into the ecology, ethology, and trophic dependencies of [[tropical animals.]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Three new monitor lizards from the Philippines identified |url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2010/05/100517070208.htm |access-date=2024-04-10 |website=ScienceDaily |language=en}}</ref> This led to the first description of several new reptile species, including ''[[Cyclemys pulchristriata]]'' {{small|[[Uwe Fritz|Fritz]], Gaulke & [[Edgar Lehr|Lehr]], 1997}}; ''[[Dendrelaphis flavescens]]'' {{small|Gaulke, 1994}}; ''[[Gekko ernstkelleri]]'' {{small|[[Herbert Rösler (herpetologist)|Rösler]], [[Cameron D. Siler|Siler]], [[Rafe Marion Brown|Brown]], [[Arnold D. Demegillo|Demegillo]] & Gaulke, 2006}}; ''[[Luperosaurus corfieldi]]'' {{small|Gaulke, Rösler & Brown, 2007}}; and ''[[Lycodon fausti]]'' {{small|Gaulke, 2002}}.

Her main interest is [[monitor lizard]]s, close relatives of the [[Komodo dragon]], which are the world's largest living lizards.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Israel |first=Brett |date=2010-05-20 |title=Huge, Colorful Monitor Lizard Species Hid in Plain Sight |url=https://www.livescience.com/6487-huge-colorful-monitor-lizard-species-hid-plain-sight.html |access-date=2024-04-10 |website=livescience.com |language=en}}</ref> She described the species ''[[Varanus mabitang]]'' {{small|Gaulke & [[Eberhard Curio|Curio]], 2001}}; ''[[Varanus palawanensis]]'' {{small|Koch, Gaulke & Böhme, 2010}}; ''[[Varanus rasmusseni]]'' {{small|Koch, Gaulke & Böhme, 2010}}; and ''[[Varanus samarensis]]'' {{small|Koch, Gaulke & Böhme, 2010}}. In 2017, she was part of the first team to describe the Philippine frog species ''[[Sanguirana]] acai'' from the islands of [[Negros]], [[Masbate]], and [[Panay]].<ref name=":1">[[Gernot Vogel|Vogel, Gernot]]; [[species:Johan van Rooijen|van Rooijen, Johan]] (2008). "Contributions to a review of the ''Dendrelaphis pictus'' ([[Johann Friedrich Gmelin|Gmelin]], 1789) complex – 2. the eastern forms". ''Herpetozoa'' '''21''' (1/2): 3–29.</ref>

Gaulke works as a consultant with national and international institutions on the status classification of endangered species and the establishment of protected areas. She is also an "extraordinary employee" at the Geobio Center at [[LMU Munich]].<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Gaulke, Maren – Geobiocenter – LMU Munich |url=https://www.geobio-center.uni-muenchen.de/experts/gaulke/index.html |access-date=2024-04-10 |website=www.geobio-center.uni-muenchen.de |language=en}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
As main author or co-author, Gaulke has published the books ''Nature Travel Guide Philippines'' (2002), ''Nature Travel Guide Australia'' (2007, with Alexander Volker Altenbach), ''Water Dragons and Sailors'' (2008, with Heiko Werning), and ''The Herpetofauna of Panay Island'', Philippines (2011). She contributed chapters to the books ''Anoxia: Evidence for Eukaryote Survival and Paleontological Strategies'' (2012) by Alexander Volker Altenbach, Joan M. Bernhard, and Joseph Seckbach and ''Varanoid Lizards of the World'' (2004) by [[Eric Pianka]], [[species:Dennis R. King|Dennis R. King]], and [[species:Ruth Allen King|Ruth Allen King]]. In addition, her scientific contributions have appeared in several international journals, including ''Hamadryad'', ''[[Zootaxa]]'',<ref>[[species:André Koch|Koch, A.]]; Gaulke, M.; [[species:Wolgang Böhme|Böhme, W.]] (2010). "Unravelling the underestimated diversity of Philippine water monitor lizards (Squamata: ''Varanus salvator'' complex), with the description of two new species and a new subspecies". ''Zootaxa'' '''2446''': 1–54. http://www.mapress.com/2010/f/z02446p054f.pdf</ref> ''Elaphe'', ''[[Pensoft Publishers|Herpetozoa]]'', ''Asiatic Herpetological Research'', ''Salamandra'' and ''[[Ichthyology & Herpetology|Copeia]]''.

==Dedication names==
In 2008, herpetologists [[Gernot Vogel]] and [[species:Johan van Rooijen|Johan van Rooijen]] named the bronzeback snake species ''[[Dendrelaphis marenae]]'' in honor of Maren Gaulke.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{EponymDictionaryReptiles}}</ref>{{rp|168}}
